tomato.visual_symptoms: Marginal chlorosis turning into scorched, necrotic brown leaf margins ('firing'); older leaves curl downwards; blotchy or uneven fruit ripening with yellow shoulder disorder.
tomato.affected_plant_part: Older and middle leaves, maturing fruits
tomato.typical_pattern: Marginal scorching and interveinal bronzing progressing from tip and margins inward, while main veins remain green longest.
tomato.possible_causes: Heavy fruit load draining available K, highly leached acidic sandy soils, excessive calcium or magnesium in soil competing for root uptake.
tomato.soil_relationship: Common in coarse-textured sandy soils and red sandy loams with low exchangeable K (<100 mg/kg).

tomato.visual_symptoms: Dark brown to black flattened sunken leathery patch at blossom end of fruit (Blossom End Rot); growing tips wither; young expanding leaves cup downward with necrotic margins.
tomato.affected_plant_part: Growing tips, young expanding leaves, fruit blossom end (Immobile)
tomato.typical_pattern: Depressed circular necrotic leathery lesion at bottom tip of tomato fruit.
tomato.possible_causes: Fluctuating soil moisture, excessive ammonium or potassium fertilization interfering with calcium uptake, acidic soils.
tomato.soil_relationship: Acidic laterite soils (pH <5.5), sandy soils with low cation exchange capacity, dry drought-stressed soils.

tomato.visual_symptoms: Leaves turn dark dull green with intense purple or reddish-violet pigmentation on veins and undersides of leaves and stems; severely restricted root system and delayed fruit setting.
tomato.affected_plant_part: Underside of older leaves first, stems
tomato.typical_pattern: Pronounced purple veinal anthocyanin accumulation on leaf undersides and petioles.
tomato.possible_causes: Cold soil temperatures restricting root uptake, P fixation in acidic laterites or alkaline calcareous soils.
tomato.soil_relationship: Red sandy loams of South India with low available Olsen-P (<10 kg/ha).

paddy.visual_symptoms: Uniform pale light-green to general chlorosis of older leaves starting from leaf tip and progressing along midrib; stunted tillering, thin erect culms, and early senescence.
paddy.typical_pattern: V-shaped chlorosis extending from leaf tip backwards along central midrib.
paddy.possible_causes: Low soil organic matter, leaching in light sandy soils, prolonged submerged denitrification in waterlogged conditions.
paddy.soil_relationship: Coarse textured sandy soils, leached floodplains, low organic carbon (<0.5%).

paddy.visual_symptoms: Brownish-red or rust-colored blotches/streaks along midrib of leaves 2-4 weeks after transplanting; lower leaves droop; plants severely stunted in uneven patches.
paddy.typical_pattern: Rust-brown coalescing pigment patches along midrib and blade.
paddy.possible_causes: Alkaline/calcareous soils (pH >7.8), continuous submergence causing insoluble zinc sulphide precipitation, excessive phosphatic fertilization.
paddy.soil_relationship: Calcareous black soils (Vertisols) of Tungabhadra and Krishna-Godavari deltas.

maize.visual_symptoms: Characteristic yellowing starting at leaf tip and progressing in an inverted V-shape along central midrib, leaving margins green longest; spindly stalks, small unfilled ears.
maize.typical_pattern: Sharp inverted V-shaped midrib chlorosis turning necrotic brown.
maize.possible_causes: Heavy rainfall leaching, waterlogging inhibiting root respiration, low organic carbon.
maize.soil_relationship: Sandy soils, poorly drained Vertisols during high rainfall.
maize.source: ICAR-IIMR & UAS Bangalore Package of Practices

maize.visual_symptoms: Broad bleached white to pale yellow bands on both sides of leaf midrib starting from base; midrib and leaf margins remain green; emerging whorl leaves almost white.
maize.typical_pattern: Broad white/cream bands on both sides of central midrib.
maize.possible_causes: High soil pH (>7.5), high available phosphorus, cold wet soils during germination.

cotton.visual_symptoms: Yellowish-white interveinal mottling followed by marginal chlorosis; leaf tips and margins curl downwards and scorch; leaves turn reddish-bronze with premature defoliation and incomplete boll opening.
cotton.affected_plant_part: Older leaves initially, migrating to top leaves during heavy boll load
cotton.typical_pattern: Marginal scorching and interveinal bronzing, leaving main veins green.
cotton.possible_causes: Heavy K depletion by high-yielding Bt cotton hybrids, sandy soils with low CEC, ill-drained saline soils.
cotton.soil_relationship: Red sandy soils (Alfisols) and weathered soils with available K <120 kg/ha.

chilli.visual_symptoms: Distinct interveinal chlorosis on older leaves: leaf veins remain green while interveinal tissue turns bright yellow to bronze; in severe cases leaf margins turn purple-red with premature leaf drop.
chilli.typical_pattern: Striking green veins on yellow leaf background on lower leaves.
chilli.possible_causes: Heavy potassium or calcium application outcompeting magnesium for root uptake; highly leached acidic sandy soils.

sugarcane.visual_symptoms: Interveinal chlorosis on youngest leaves: veins remain sharply green while intervening tissue becomes bleached ivory-white or pale yellow; whole cane tops appear bleached white in severe patches.
sugarcane.typical_pattern: Sharp parallel green veins on bleached white leaf blade.
sugarcane.possible_causes: Calcareous alkaline soils containing high free calcium carbonate (CaCO3) causing iron precipitation as insoluble ferric hydroxide; high bicarbonate water.
sugarcane.soil_relationship: Calcareous black Vertisols of North Karnataka, Western Tamil Nadu, Rayalaseema.

coconut.visual_symptoms: Translucent yellow to orange-brown spots on leaflets of older fronds; leaflets develop severe marginal necrosis and necrotic tip drying; fronds look scorched and die prematurely; slender tapering trunk.
coconut.typical_pattern: Orange-yellow spotting coalescing into dry ragged leaflet margins.
coconut.possible_causes: High potassium demand of perennial palms; extensive leaching in sandy coastal soils and laterites.
coconut.soil_relationship: Coastal sands, laterites of Kerala and Karnataka with K2O <100 kg/ha.
